The fundamental watersheds that FWA_Upstream reaches from some of them

Source: R/wet_ws_closure.R
wet_ws_reach.Rd

Which rows of ws lie in the FWA_Upstream set of at least one of the rows from (each counting itself), by the same ranges wet_upstream_sums() sums over, with irregularly coded polygons from irregular_pairs. Over an upstream-closed ws such as wet_ws_closure()'s, those rows are the least set that gives the from rows their sums: wet_upstream_sums() over them, with irregular_pairs cut to the id_up rows kept, gives the from rows the same sums as over all of ws, up to the order the doubles are added in.

Usage

wet_ws_reach(ws, from, irregular_pairs = NULL)

Arguments

ws

data.frame with watershed_feature_id, wscode and localcode (FWA ltree codes as text).

from

Logical, one per row of ws: the rows whose upstream sets to join.

irregular_pairs

Optional data.frame(watershed_feature_id, id_up), as wet_upstream_sums() takes it. Without it, irregularly coded rows are left out with a warning, as wet_upstream_sums() leaves them out.

Value

Logical, one per row of ws.

Examples

ws <- data.frame(watershed_feature_id = 1:5,
                 wscode = c("100", "100", "100.000300", "100.000300", "100.000700"),
                 localcode = c("100", "100.000500", "100.000300", "100.000300.000010",
                               "100.000700"))
# row 2 sits on the main stem above position 000500: it reaches itself
# and the tributary at 000700, not row 1 or the tributary at 000300
wet_ws_reach(ws, ws$watershed_feature_id == 2)
#> [1] FALSE  TRUE FALSE FALSE  TRUE
